title: Signal and Archive
premise: Gideon Iversen, a xenolinguist haunted by dreams that arrive in no human tongue, is hauling cargo through contested orbits when a derelict warship surfaces from deep space carrying a crew who have aged backward — living proof that someone has weaponized time. Among them is Vess Okonkwo, a soldier who remembers a future Gideon hasn't lived, and the two become bound by a message encoded in the ship's signal: a truth about the war that both governments will kill to bury. As fleets converge and the message begins rewriting Gideon's memories in exchange for every translation, he and Vess must choose between loyalty to the people who saved them and the truth that could end the war. In the end, Gideon broadcasts the message at the cost of his own past — forgetting Vess entirely — and the ceasefire holds, built on a sacrifice no one remembers he made.
about_author: Odile Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing signals she was never allowed to answer. She writes near-future fiction about people who listen for a living, and lives on a decommissioned ferry with an unreasonable number of shortwave receivers.

chapters.title: Dead Orbit Freight
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Establishes the hauler Meridian's Bell, its small crew, and the contested shipping lanes of the Kestrel Corridor. Gideon translates a routine customs ping and realizes he dreamed last night in a language that doesn't exist. Beat: quiet unease beneath routine competence.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A distress beacon leads them to the warship Anemoi, missing for thirty years, drifting intact. The boarding party finds crew who are biologically younger than when they left. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as the implications land.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Vess Okonkwo's POV, first appearance. She wakes from temporal stasis remembering a ceasefire that hasn't happened, a Gideon she's never met, and her own court-martial. She lies to her rescuers about what she knows. Beat: disorientation weaponized into survival.

chapters.title: Customs and Casualties
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A Kestrel patrol impounds the Anemoi's black box; the crew of the Meridian's Bell is conscripted as 'neutral carriers' to ferry evidence to the admiralty. Gideon recognizes fragments of the box's signal — it's the language from his dreams. Beat: the personal collides with the political.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, flashback-heavy. How Gideon lost his linguistic career after a first-contact incident he still can't explain, and why he dreams in alien tongues. Vess watches him translate and goes pale. Beat: grief excavated; Vess recognizes him from her future.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hull
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She reveals a fragment of truth: the Anemoi didn't get lost — it was sent through an experimental fold, and the message is the price the future paid to send it back. She asks Gideon to decode it before the admiralty can. Beat: trust offered as a gamble.

chapters.title: Convoy Ambush
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The convoy is attacked by separatists who want the black box destroyed. Gideon's captain dies shielding the data core. Gideon decodes his first phrase under fire: 'Tell them what we buried.' Beat: loss hardens resolve into mission.

chapters.title: Admiralty Station Vireo
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The survivors reach the naval stronghold and are celebrated as heroes — and quietly separated. Gideon is offered reinstatement if he hands over his translations. He recognizes the admiral's aide from Vess's described future. Beat: seduction of legitimacy.

chapters.title: What the Future Paid
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, confined to quarters. She reconstructs the Anemoi's mission log from memory: the fold didn't just move the ship, it traded years — the crew's past for the message's passage. Every translation Gideon does is drawing from his own memory. Beat: horror of the mechanism revealed.

chapters.title: The Language That Eats
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Decoding accelerates; Gideon loses his mother's face, then his sister's name, each phrase costing a memory. He hides it from Vess. Beat: the price of truth made intimate and irreversible.

chapters.title: Two Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She escapes confinement and finds proof both sides knew the fold weapon worked — the war is being sustained to hide the experiment's casualties. She must choose: flee with Gideon or finish the message. Beat: loyalty fractures along the fault line of truth.

chapters.title: The Aide's Offer
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The admiral's aide reveals she is from the Anemoi's original crew — aged forward, not back — and offers Gideon restoration of his lost memories in exchange for a doctored translation. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Recaptured, Vess is interrogated using a memory-extraction rig. Gideon, watching through the feed, hears her describe their future partnership — including his sacrifice. Beat: devastating dramatic irony; he now knows the cost and chooses to continue.

chapters.title: Half a Message
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon and a sympathetic engineer break Vess out, but the decoded half of the message is enough to start a war if released alone. They steal the Meridian's Bell and run. Beat: point of no return; fugitive momentum.

chapters.title: The Fold's Graveyard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Pursued by both fleets, they shelter among the debris of failed fold experiments — thousands of ships, crews aged to dust or infancy. The scale of the cover-up becomes undeniable. Beat: righteous fury and shared purpose.

chapters.title: Translation as Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final phrases require memories Gideon treasures most: his reason for becoming a linguist, his first language. He begins the last translation knowing he'll end it a stranger to himself. Beat: tragic resolve, love expressed as loss.

chapters.title: The Fleet Converges
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Both armadas arrive at the broadcast relay. Vess negotiates a ten-minute window by threatening to release the doctored version the admiralty fears. Beat: brinkmanship; the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. Gideon broadcasts the complete message — the truth of the buried crews, the manufactured war — as his memories unravel mid-transmission. He finishes in a language he no longer understands, not knowing who Vess is. Beat: triumph and erasure in the same breath.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Relay
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Fleets stand down as the evidence spreads through every channel. Vess holds Gideon, who looks at her with polite incomprehension. She chooses not to tell him what he gave up. Beat: victory shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Man Who Forgot the War
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Months later, Gideon lives quietly, dreams dreamless, decorated for something he can't remember doing. Vess appears in his life as a stranger — a fellow traveler on his cargo run. Beat: bittersweet domesticity, the ache of a blank space.

chapters.title: Archive
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess keeps a private archive: recordings of Gideon's lost memories, the message, the names of the fold's casualties. She visits the memorial and adds one name no one else knows to honor. Beat: memory preserved against forgetting; love as custodianship.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Tongues
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, final chapter. Gideon dreams, for the first time in years — not in alien languages, but in his own voice, saying a name he doesn't recognize: Vess. He wakes and, on instinct, sets a course she once described. Beat: hope; the self endures in fragments, and chooses again.
